name: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Definitions and ACR Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (PR3-ANCA or MPO-ANCA) in serum
Biopsy showing necrotizing vasculitis of small to medium vessels with few or no immune deposits
Clinical evidence of systemic small vessel vasculitis affecting respiratory tract, kidneys, or other organs
Exclusion of other causes of vasculitis such as infections or other autoimmune diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ANCA positivity plus compatible clinical features and histopathological confirmation of necrotizing vasculitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, serological, and histopathological data.

pathognomonic.notes: Often presents with hematuria and proteinuria
May cause hemoptysis and respiratory distress

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of circulating anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (PR3-ANCA or MPO-ANCA)

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including fever and weight loss
searchTerms: fever, weight loss, and night sweats
general symptoms like tiredness and fever
systemic illness signs including weight loss

common.notes: Peripheral nerve involvement causing asymmetric neuropathy

occasional.notes: Inflammation of the sclera or episclera
Due to vasculitis affecting mesenteric vessels
searchTerms: stomach pain from poor blood flow

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac involvement including pericarditis or myocarditis

occasional.notes: Seen on imaging in granulomatosis with polyangiitis subtype

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema secondary to renal impairment
occasional.notes: Due to nephrotic syndrome or renal failure
searchTerms: swelling in legs from kidney issues
leg swelling due to kidney problems

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system vasculitis causing stroke or seizures
searchTerms: seizures due to brain vessel disease
bleeding in lungs without kidney damage

laboratory: Urinalysis showing hematuria and red cell casts
imaging: Chest CT showing pulmonary nodules, cavitations, or alveolar hemorrhage
Sinus CT demonstrating mucosal thickening or bony destruction
Renal ultrasound may show normal or small kidneys in chronic disease
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; possible HLA associations
other: Histopathology showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation or pauci-immune vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of granulomatous inflammation on biopsy
Positive ANA and other lupus-specific antibodies

redFlags: Mononeuritis multiplex or rapidly progressive neuropathy
references: Jennette JC, Falk RJ, Bacon PA, et al. 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum. 2013 Jan;65(1):1-11.
Yates M, Watts RA, Bajema IM, et al. EULAR/ERA-EDTA recommendations for the management of ANCA-associated vasculitis. Ann Rheum Dis. 2016 Mar;75(9):1583-94.
Kallenberg CGM. Pathogenesis and treatment of ANCA-associated vasculitides. Clin Exp Rheumatol. 2015;33(4 Suppl 92):S11-4.
